While Frey stated he didn't want anything to "prematurely undermine" the investigation led by Chief Medaria Arradondo, Frey met with the family once more on Friday.
"I offered our apology on behalf of the city to whomever they would choose to accept it from," Frey said outside City Hall in his two-hour meeting with the family.
According to court documents, investigators searched for phone data related to the phones of 4-year veteran vehicle-crime detective Matthew Harrity and a nearby officer, about a week after the July 15 shooting.
Executive director Andy Stoute of the Minnesota Chiefs of Police Association chose not to comment on the officer who requested to search his married father's computer.
